podcast.title: Fake Production Credits in UK (1962)
podcast.body: Shell Tauhmey, an engineer from Los Angeles, came to the UK in 1962 and sought work in the music industry. A friend, Nick Vennett, provided him with a stack of acetates of recent Capitol Records productions (including "Surf and Safari" by The Beach Boys and "Music in the Air" by Lou Rawls) and suggested he "pretend to produce them" to secure work. Tauhmey then presented these to Dick Rowe at Decca, who hired him to produce records, starting with hits like "Charmaine" by The Bachelors. "Tauhmey was a good friend of Nick Vennett, and Vennett gave him a stack of acetates of recent capital records that he produced, and told him that he could pretend to produce them if he got in work."

podcast.title: Death Details - November 13, 2024
podcast.body: Shel Talmy died on November 13th, 2024, at the age of 87, after suffering a stroke. "He had a stroke and died at the age of 87 on November 13th."

podcast.title: Disputed Original "You Really Got Me" Production
podcast.body: Shell Tauhmey produced the initial recording of "You Really Got Me," which Ray and Dave Davis strongly disliked, claiming he "overproduced it, turning it into a full specter sound alike, and drenched the whole thing with echo." Tauhmey, however, defended his version, asserting that the main difference was a slower tempo and that it was a "very different but equally valid take on the song." "Towney for his part says that that's not the case, that the main difference was that the song was taken much slower, and that it was a very different but equally valid take on the song."

podcast.title: Producer for The Kinks and The Who
podcast.body: Shel Talmy was an influential producer who worked on early records for prominent bands such as The Kinks and The Who. "Tell Shami produced early records for the kinks and the who."
